NASA ACME one-pager states BRE is focused on fire prevention; brief says 'study of materials flammability'
PSI-20 subResearchArea 'Flames of Gaseous Fuels'; objective names gaseous CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2; brief confirms 'burned gaseous fuels'
PSI-20 objective names CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2; experimental table lists 100% C2H4, 50% C2H4, 100% CH4 fuel bottles
PSI-20 objective: porous circular burners 25 and 50 mm; experimental table Burner Size column has 25 and 50; ACME one-pager describes flat porous burner
PSI-20 experimentHardware 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'; brief: six ACME experiments used same modular hardware in CIR

PSI-20 experimentHardware mentions ACME hardware; ACME one-pager details: two heat-flux transducers per burner, surface thermocouple, internal porous-burner pressure, three mass flow controllers, ACME avionics
Brief states six ACME experiments share CIR hardware; psi-map.json lists five other ACME IDs (acme-cld-flame, acme-e-field, acme-s-flames, acme-cfi-g, acme-flame-design)
PSI-20 experimental table CSV: Oxygen Conc values across 18 rows are 21, 25, 26.5, 34, 40 (after dropping 3400% and 2100% data-entry errors). Min 21, max 40 matches extracted record.

Extracted range 8.2-14.7 psi comes from the three NASA atmospheres listed in PSI-20 objective (14.7/21%, 10.2/26.5%, 8.2/34%). CSV note states 'chamber pressures were also varied but are not identified in this summary table.' Actual per-test pressures unknown; the range reflects planned atmospheres, not measured test pressures.
PSI-20 objective and approach describe 'quiescent microgravity ambient'; brief: 'still atmospheres'; CSV has no flow column. Recorded as 0 cm/s (no imposed flow) with appropriate note.
PSI-20 projectType 'Microgravity Investigation'; flightProgram ISS; brief confirms no partial-gravity data in PSI

PSI-20 objective: O2/N2 ambients tested; O2/CO2 ambients 'desired' (planned, not confirmed flown). CSV note: 'diluted with nitrogen'. CO2 diluent not confirmed in flown tests; medium confidence appropriate.

PSI-20 experimental table varies burner size (25/50), fuel bottle (100% C2H4, 50% C2H4, 100% CH4), oxygen concentration (21, 25, 26.5, 34, 40%); objective states pressures, diluent choice, fuel mixtures varied; table note confirms pressures varied.
PSI-20 approach: ambient is quiescent across tests; fuel flow controlled from burner heat flux/temperature to emulate condensed-phase vaporization.

ACME one-pager: two heat-flux transducers per burner, surface thermocouple, internal pressure, radiometers, color/CH*/OH* cameras, gas chromatograph, SAMS-II. PSI-20 approach confirms burner surface temperature and heat flux measured.

Brief: BRE studied materials flammability in still atmospheres. PSI-20 researchImpacts: quasi-steady burning of PMMA/Nylon in microgravity without airflow, elevated-O2 atmospheres sustained combustion while 21% O2 self-extinguished, suggests cone calorimeter (NASA Test 2) for material screening.

PSI-20 researchImpacts recommends increased use of cone calorimeter (NASA Test 2), an Earth fire-test instrument; extracted record correctly marks confidence 'inferred' and notes terrestrial benefit implication.
PSI-20.json lists 16 publications with DOIs; extracted record includes first 6 with valid DOI links. Note acknowledges omission for brevity.

summary: Record is well-supported by PSI-20.json, experimental table CSV, ACME one-pager, and challenge brief. Two fields rated 'partly': pressure_psi range reflects planned NASA atmospheres from objective, not measured per-test pressures (CSV notes pressures varied but unlisted); diluents includes CO2 which was only 'desired' in objective, not confirmed flown. All other fields supported. No contradictions found.
